claims: Joby links electric vertical-flight technology to short-range mobility and potentially dual-use logistics, but the binding path to human transport value remains certification -> manufacturing -> vertiport/airspace integration -> reliable high-utilization operations.
Toyota production-system transfer and conforming-aircraft progress can reduce manufacturing/certification risk, while infrastructure and utilization become successor bottlenecks after certification.
causalEdges: battery/eVTOL technology -> certified aircraft -> scaled manufacturing -> vertiport/airspace network -> passenger/logistics service -> time-efficient mobility need
manufacturing know-how -> production repeatability -> fleet availability
substitutes: ground ride-hailing and premium car service
counterfactuals: If certification succeeds but vertiports or utilization lag, aircraft capability does not automatically become a scalable mobility network.
falsifiers: inability to manufacture conforming aircraft at repeatable economics
commercial utilization insufficient for viable service economics

claims: Final-stage certification progress is not approval; conforming aircraft and factory footprint are not proof of achieved production rate or unit economics.
Autonomy demonstrations expand optionality but should not be counted as near-term passenger-service approval or revenue; infrastructure and capital intensity can become commercialization constraints.
unknowns: commercial aircraft unit cost and production rate
improvementPaths: demonstrate repeatable production and delivery cadence
publish operating utilization and route economics after launch
falsifiers: certification plus repeatable fleet production and strong utilization would materially weaken the core commercialization challenge
